links.outcome: Comparison of open-source Llama3 models against proprietary GPT-4o models on same annotation data
links.effect: GPT-4o highest accuracy 97.9%; Llama3.1-405b 97.1%, GPT-4o-mini 96.9%, Llama3-8b 96.9%, Llama3.1-70b 96.0%; open-source rivals proprietary
links.quote: Small, open-source LLMs can accurately annotate Danish trauma radiology reports when supported by effective prompt engineering, achieving accuracy levels that rival proprietary competitors.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering on a development split to improve open-source LLM annotation accuracy
Using locally hosted open-source LLMs as a privacy-conscious alternative to proprietary models

links.quote: GPT-4o achieved the highest overall diagnostic accuracy at 97.9% (95% CI: 97.3% – 98.5%), followed by Llama3.1-405b (97.1% (95% CI: 96.4% – 97.8%)), GPT-4o-mini (96.9% (95% CI: 96.2% – 97.6%)), Llama3-8b (96.9% (95% CI: 95.9% – 97.3%)), and Llama3.1-70b (96.0% (95% CI: 95.2% – 96.8%)).

links.effect: Semantic Confusion was most frequent, with 53.2% to 59.4% of misclassifications.
links.quote: Of the error types, Semantic Confusion was the most frequent, with 53.2% to 59.4% of misclassifications.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering for radiology report annotation improved Llama3-8b Match-score from 77.8% to 94.3%.
